## Step One: Create a project locally

Use `create_visc_project()` to create an analysis project in a location you can
write to. The example uses a home-directory path; replace it with your local or
institutional project location as appropriate.

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(VISCtemplates)
create_visc_project("~/VDCnnnAnalysis")
```

The directory name should match the CAVD name with `Analysis` at the end, for
example `Gallo477Analysis`. Some studies have other trial-protocol names; use the
CAVD name for this convention.

By default, `package = FALSE`: this creates an RStudio analysis project, not an
R package. The principal generated files and directories are:

```text
VDCnnnAnalysis/
|- .github/
|  +- pull_request_template.md    # GitHub pull request template
|- .gitignore                    # File types ignored by Git
|- docs/
|  +- background.Rmd             # Shared study background
|  +- objectives.Rmd              # Shared study objectives
|  +- bibliography.bib           # Project-level bibliography
|  +- presentations/             # Protocol presentations
|- inst/
|  +- WORDLIST                   # Custom words for spell checking
|- R/
|  +- colors-and-shapes.R        # Shared figure colors and shapes
|  +- study_schema.R             # Study-design table function
|- README.md                     # Edit this project guide directly
|- VDCnnnAnalysis.Rproj           # RStudio project file
```

Additional supporting files may be created by usethis. The temporary project
`README.Rmd` is rendered to `README.md` and then removed. Edit the resulting
`README.md` directly; this differs from maintaining the VISCtemplates package's
own README, whose source is `README.Rmd`.

If you specifically need an R package project, opt in:

```{r eval=FALSE}
create_visc_project("~/Gallo477Analysis", package = TRUE)
```

Package mode also initializes package-specific metadata such as `DESCRIPTION`
and `NAMESPACE`; these are not part of the default analysis-project setup.

Project creation normally opens a new RStudio session. Continue in the created
project, loading `VISCtemplates` again in the new session when needed.

## Step Two: GitHub

Initialize Git in the new project and create a private repository in the
FredHutch organization:

```{r eval=FALSE}
usethis::use_git()
usethis::use_github(organisation = "FredHutch", private = TRUE, protocol = "ssh")
```

For the SSH workflow, set up an [SSH key](https://happygitwithr.com/ssh-keys)
first. Verify that the repository is private and grant the appropriate
FredHutch/vidd-visc team access. In repository settings, configure branch
protection or rulesets for the actual default branch (usually `main`), requiring
pull request review before merging. GitHub settings labels may change.

## Step Three: Customize shared documentation

1. `README.md`: add project guidance, data locations, and Study-Specific Training
   (SST) information.
2. `docs/`: customize the shared background and objectives, and maintain the
   project bibliography.
3. `R/colors-and-shapes.R` and `R/study_schema.R`: adapt colors, shapes, and the
   study-design table to the study.

## Step Four: Start analysis work

After completing setup on the project's default branch, create a report branch.
For example, run this command in a terminal:

```sh
git checkout -b bama-analysis
```

Then create a report from R in the active analysis project:

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(VISCtemplates)
use_visc_report(
  report_name = "VDCnnn_BAMA_PTreport_interim_blinded",
  path = "BAMA",
  report_type = "bama"
)
```

The available `report_type` values are `"empty"`, `"generic"`, `"bama"`,
`"nab"`, and `"adcc"`. Use `"empty"` for a minimal skeleton, `"generic"` for
non-assay-specific PT methods, or an assay-specific option for its methods text.
Non-empty reports receive methods files in a report-level `child-docs/` folder.

Each report folder receives a `README.md`. If the assay directory does not yet
exist, `use_visc_report()` also creates that directory and an assay-level
`README.md`. Shared study text remains in the project's `docs/` directory.

See the report-template vignette for details:

```{r eval=FALSE}
vignette("using_pdf_and_word_template", package = "VISCtemplates")
```

## Spell check

Project creation saves common scientific words in `inst/WORDLIST`. Use the
[spelling package](https://docs.ropensci.org/spelling/) to check report text and
maintain the word list. R Markdown spell checking targets prose rather than R
code chunks.

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("spelling")
spelling::spell_check_files(
  "BAMA/VDCnnn_BAMA_PTreport_interim_blinded/VDCnnn_BAMA_PTreport_interim_blinded.Rmd"
)
```
